name: SylvaDB
tagline: Web-based relaxed-schema graph data manager for humanities researchers, built on Django over Neo4j.
description: Sylva, from the CulturePlex Lab, is a graph database management system aimed at researchers who do not program, especially in the digital humanities. In the browser you define a flexible, relaxed schema of node and relationship types, enter or import data collaboratively, explore it visually and run queries and network analytics, while the storage itself sits in a pluggable graph backend such as Neo4j, Neo4j Spatial or Blueprints/Rexster. It was offered as a hosted service at sylvadb.com and as AGPL-licensed Django code. The hosted service is offline and the code has not changed since January 2016.
statusNote: Hosted sylvadb.com is offline and the AGPL code on GitHub has had no commits since January 2016. Neo4j with its browser tools is the practical successor.

pricing.notes: Source is AGPL; the hosted sylvadb.com plans are no longer available.

scale.notes: Bounded by the underlying graph backend and a single Django deployment.

strengths: Schema design, data entry and querying entirely in the browser, aimed at non-programmers
Relaxed schemas let researchers evolve models as their sources change
Pluggable graph backends including Neo4j and Neo4j Spatial
weaknesses: Dormant since 2016 with dated Django and Neo4j dependencies
A management layer, not a storage engine, so performance depends on the backend
